content: An ethyl group in chemistry refers to an alkyl functional group that is derived from ethane (C2H6). Its chemical formula is -C2H5, and it is frequently abbreviated as -Et. During the mid-20th century in North America, the term ethyl was commonly used to describe high-performance commercial gasoline that contained lead. This designation originated from the Ethyl Corporation, a company that produced tetraethyl lead, an organometallic compound used as an antiknock agent in gasoline. The process of ethylation involves the introduction of the ethyl functional group, C2H5, into a compound.
